spots.name: Jardins de Laribal
spots.blurb: Terraced gardens on the flank of Montjuïc, laid out around 1917-1922 by Forestier and Rubió i Tudurí with pergolas, tiled stairways, trickling water channels and the Font del Gat midway down. Most visitors hurry past to the Fundació Joan Miró or the Teatre Grec, so the shaded benches under the pines stay quiet. Drift between the levels with a book; the lower terraces catch the breeze off the port.
spots.tips: Enter from the upper gate near the Fundació Joan Miró (Avinguda de Miramar side) and work downhill toward the Teatre Grec; the benches around the Font del Gat are the shadiest. Gates close at dusk like the other Montjuïc gardens.

safety.note: Well-kept municipal garden on a busy cultural hillside; quiet but not deserted, and it closes at dusk.

spots.verifyNote: Real, long-established municipal garden, kept from reviewer knowledge; no search possible. Fixed the Font del Gat position (mid-slope, not the top) and the entrance description.

spots.name: Parc del Laberint d'Horta
spots.blurb: Barcelona's oldest surviving garden: an 18th-century neoclassical estate with a cypress hedge maze, a romantic upper garden, moss-covered fountains and a long canal. Entry is capped (a few hundred people at a time), so it never feels busy, and the terraces above the maze are usually silent. Locals come here to sit under the trees with a book.
spots.tips: Small entry fee (around EUR 2) but free on Wednesdays and Sundays; a weekday morning gives near-empty paths. Metro Mundet (L3), then a five-minute walk uphill.

safety.note: Ticketed, staffed garden with limited entry; very calm.

spots.verifyNote: Well-known historic garden; Wikipedia title kept because the reviewer is highly confident of the exact English article name, though no search confirmation was possible this session. Softened the visitor-cap and price wording.

spots.name: Bunkers del Carmel
spots.blurb: The old anti-aircraft battery on the Turó de la Rovira gives the widest 360-degree view in the city, from Tibidabo round to the sea. It is no longer a secret and sunset draws a crowd, but arrive mid-morning on a weekday and you share the concrete platforms with a few neighbours walking dogs. The council has fenced the site and closes it at night after years of late-night parties.
spots.tips: Take bus V17 or 119 to skip the steep climb, and go early morning for empty terraces. Check current opening times before a sunset visit; the site is gated after dark.
spots.hours: daytime only; gated after dark (check current times)

safety.note: Busy, well-known public viewpoint at golden hour; keep phones and bags close in the crowd. Night access is closed by the city, so plan the walk down before closing.

spots.verifyNote: Real, heavily visited public viewpoint (MUHBA site). Wikipedia title set to null: the exact English article title could not be confirmed this session (may be Turó de la Rovira). Gated closing times unverified; kept as check current times.

spots.name: Carretera de les Aigües
spots.blurb: A flat, car-free gravel track that follows an old water pipeline along the Collserola hillside a few hundred metres above the city. Runners and cyclists own it at dawn; the rest of the day you can find a bench with the whole skyline and the sea below and nobody within earshot. It is the easiest wild-feeling escape from Barcelona.
spots.tips: Take the FGC to Peu del Funicular and ride the Vallvidrera funicular to the Carretera de les Aigües stop, then walk in either direction. There is no lighting, so go for sunrise or be back down by dark.

safety.note: No lighting after dark and few people once the runners leave; walk it in daylight, be back at the funicular before nightfall and carry water in summer.

spots.verifyNote: Real, popular public trail in Collserola park; kept with caution for the unlit hillside. Coordinates nudged to the funicular stop.

spots.name: Espigó del Bac de Roda
spots.blurb: A stone breakwater that juts into the sea between Bogatell and Mar Bella, the beaches locals favour over Barceloneta. Walk to the end and sit with the anglers and early swimmers; the sun comes straight up out of the water. It is the closest thing Barcelona has to a quiet pier.
spots.tips: Bring something to sit on, the surface is uneven. The promenade behind it is lit and lively on summer evenings, but the breakwater itself is dark after sunset.

safety.note: Unlit, unrailed breakwater: use it in daylight, skip it in rough seas or strong onshore wind, and stay on the lit promenade after dark.

spots.verifyNote: Real breakwater at the seaward end of Carrer de Bac de Roda; kept but raised to caution because it is an unrailed rock structure with no lighting. Trimmed the claim that visitors never reach these beaches.

spots.name: Plaça de la Virreina
spots.blurb: Gràcia's gentlest square: a church facade, plane trees, a couple of unhurried terraces and neighbours on the benches until late. It has none of the noise of Plaça del Sol a few streets away, so it is where people come to talk quietly or sit alone with a coffee. Evenings are lit and lively without being loud.
spots.tips: The benches under the trees on the church side are the quietest; take a coffee from a terrace if you want a table. Metro Fontana (L3).

safety.note: Residential square with terraces open late; well lit and populated in the evening.

spots.verifyNote: Real, well-known Gràcia square (church of Sant Joan); kept from reviewer knowledge.

spots.name: Plaça de Sant Felip Neri
spots.blurb: A tiny baroque square tucked behind the cathedral, with a fountain, trees and a church facade still pocked by a 1938 bombing. It is well known now, but its enclosed shape muffles the Gothic Quarter noise, and early in the morning or late in the evening it is often empty. Sit on the fountain rim and let the city fade out.
spots.tips: Come before 10am or after 9pm; midday brings tour groups and the school on the square lets out at lunchtime. Reach it via Carrer de Sant Sever from the cathedral.

safety.note: Central and lit at night; as in all the Gothic Quarter lanes, keep phones and bags close.

spots.verifyNote: Real, famous square; Wikipedia title kept because the reviewer is highly confident of the exact English article name, though no search confirmation was possible this session.

spots.name: Plaça de la Concòrdia
spots.blurb: The old village square of Les Corts, with a 19th-century clock tower, a few cafe terraces and pensioners on the benches. It sits a short walk from Camp Nou yet feels like a small town, and in the evening it is one of the calmest places in the city to sit with a drink. Few visitors find it.
spots.tips: The terraces face the tower; the benches in the middle are free and shaded by mid-afternoon. Metro Les Corts or Maria Cristina (L3), then a short walk.

safety.note: Quiet residential square with terraces open into the evening; well lit.

spots.verifyNote: Real historic square of the former town of Les Corts; kept from reviewer knowledge. Trimmed the nobody-knows-it claim.

spots.name: Parc del Turó del Putxet
spots.blurb: A small hill park above Sant Gervasi whose summit terrace looks over the whole city to the sea, with Tibidabo at your back. Unlike the Bunkers it draws only neighbours walking dogs, so the benches at the top are usually free at golden hour. Winding paths through pines and a few open terraces cover the rest of the hill.
spots.tips: Enter from Carrer de Manacor near the Putxet FGC station and follow the paths uphill; the mirador is at the very top. The park closes at dusk.

safety.note: Municipal park in a quiet residential area; gates close at dusk.

spots.verifyNote: Real gated municipal hill park; kept from reviewer knowledge. Removed the unverified picnic-tables detail.

spots.name: Jardins del Palau de Pedralbes
spots.blurb: The formal gardens of the old royal palace: cedars, a lily pond, a bamboo grove and a small fountain attributed to Gaudí that most people walk straight past. The lawns are open for lying down, which is rare in Barcelona, and the uptown location keeps numbers low. It is a classic spot for a shaded afternoon nap.
spots.tips: Enter from Avinguda Diagonal (metro Palau Reial, L3); the lawns behind the palace are the quietest. Gates close at dusk.

safety.note: Fenced municipal garden, calm and family-friendly.

spots.verifyNote: Real municipal garden around the palace; Wikipedia title (palace article, which sits in these gardens) kept because the reviewer is highly confident of the exact English article name; no search confirmation was possible this session.

spots.name: Laie Llibreria Cafè
spots.blurb: A serious bookshop on Carrer de Pau Claris with a cafe upstairs where nobody minds if you nurse one coffee for a couple of hours. The room is calm, the light is good, and the clientele is mostly people reading rather than working. Browse downstairs, then carry a new book up with you.
spots.tips: Weekday afternoons are quietest; lunchtime fills with office workers. Closed Sundays; confirm cafe hours on the site.

safety.note: Central, staffed bookshop in the Eixample.

spots.verifyNote: Long-running bookshop-cafe at Pau Claris 85; kept from reviewer knowledge, hours unverified and marked check site.

spots.name: Federal Café
spots.blurb: An Australian-style cafe on Carrer del Parlament that has been Sant Antoni's laptop refuge since 2010. Big windows, decent food and a small plant-filled roof terrace make it easy to lose an afternoon. Weekdays are calm; weekend brunch is another story.
spots.tips: Come on a weekday morning for a window seat or the roof terrace; laptops are welcome outside peak brunch hours. Metro Sant Antoni (L2) or Poble Sec (L3).

safety.note: Busy, friendly neighbourhood cafe on a lively street.

spots.verifyNote: Well-known cafe at Carrer del Parlament 39; kept from reviewer knowledge. Removed the plugs claim; hours unverified and marked check site.

spots.name: Biblioteca Jaume Fuster
spots.blurb: Gràcia's modern public library, an award-winning folded-roof building by Josep Llinàs on Plaça de Lesseps with a big airy reading floor, a newspaper lounge and a terrace. It is free to walk in and sit, no card needed, and the upstairs tables are quiet enough to read or work for hours. Locals treat it as a shared living room.
spots.tips: The upper floors are quieter than the ground floor; the terrace is good on warm evenings. Metro Lesseps (L3); check weekend and summer hours before going.
spots.hours: varies (check site); typically Mon-Fri 10am-9pm, shorter Sat

safety.note: Staffed public library, open into the evening on weekdays.

spots.verifyNote: Real municipal library (opened 2005); kept from reviewer knowledge, hours unverified.

spots.name: Mercat del Born
spots.blurb: A 19th-century iron market hall (now El Born Centre de Cultura i Memòria) whose floor is an excavated slice of the 1700s city, viewed from walkways around the edge. Walking in and looking down at the ruins is free, and the hall is cool, high and echoing. It is one of the best rainy-day places in the old town to slow down and think.
spots.tips: Access to the hall and walkways is free; only the exhibitions charge. Closed Mondays; there is a cafe inside the hall for waiting out rain.
spots.hours: Tue-Sun 10am-8pm (shorter in winter); Mon closed (check site)

safety.note: Staffed cultural centre in a busy neighbourhood.

spots.verifyNote: Real cultural centre (El Born CCM); Wikipedia title set to null because the exact English article title could not be confirmed this session (may be El Born Centre de Cultura i Memòria). Trimmed unverified bench and cafe-location details.
